title: Knock Knock
summary: Overnight, one address tried a few passwords against every account on the office PC - and one of them opened. Find the door that gave way and the scheduled task left behind it.
story: {{CO}} (made up) keeps its accounts PC, {{PC}}, on 10.10.24.0/24. The Security log is suddenly full of failed sign-ins. You sit at soc on the same network with the PC's administrator password: {{ADMPW}} (winrm-shell -i 10.10.24.30 -u Administrator -p {{ADMPW}}).
goal: Find the address that tried the passwords, the one account it got into and the scheduled task it created; capture the flag beside the task's script; then switch that account off and remove the task before it runs.
skills: the Security log (4625, 4624, 4698), password spraying, Get-ScheduledTask, Unregister-ScheduledTask, Disable-LocalUser

flags.name: The flag beside the task's script

questions.explain: Every 4625 (failed sign-in) comes from this Source Network Address.

questions.ask: Which account did it get into?
questions.explain: The only 4624 (successful sign-in) from that address.

questions.ask: What is the name of the scheduled task it created?
questions.explain: Event 4698 (a scheduled task was created) names it, and Get-ScheduledTask lists it.

tasks.name: Switch off the account that was broken into
tasks.explain: Disable-LocalUser -Name {{VIC}} (until its owner picks a new, strong password)

attacker.note: The scheduled task ran and copied the accounts share into its folder, ready to be taken.

hints.text: A few failures for each of many accounts from one address is password spraying: one or two common passwords tried everywhere, hoping one person chose it. Read event 4625 (failed) and 4624 (succeeded) in the Security log: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName='Security'; Id=4625 } | Format-List TimeCreated, Message.

Of all the accounts tried, only one has a 4624 from the same address. What did it do next? Event 4698 means a scheduled task was created; Get-ScheduledTask lists tasks, and (Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName NAME).Actions shows what one runs.
The flag is in the task's folder under C:\ProgramData. Clean up: Disable-LocalUser -Name {{VIC}} and Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName {{TASK}} -Confirm:$false.
